item.title: Titles, Blood and Breakthroughs at CareFirst Arena
item.description: Davis Boxing Promotions' "The Grind and the Glory" fight card featured nine matches, including a hard-fought win by Erick Rosado over previously undefeated Christopher Glenn, a unanimous decision win by Greg Outlaw over Michael Lee, and a first-round knockout by Keith Saunders Jr. over Lucius Johnson. The post Titles, Blood and Breakthroughs at CareFirst Arena appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: The Great American Departure Gains Speed
item.description: Americans are leaving the U.S. in record numbers, driven by political instability, gun violence, health care costs, and economic anxiety, while immigrants continue to anchor the economy and workforce in cities like Washington, D.C. The post The Great American Departure Gains Speed appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: TILGHMAN: Why Safe Passage Is Personal — and Why It’s About All of Our Children
item.description: Safe Passage is a community-driven initiative in Prince George's County, Maryland, which provides trained, visible adults along student travel routes to ensure student safety and security. The post TILGHMAN: Why Safe Passage Is Personal — and Why It’s About All of Our Children appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Black Voters Demand Results and Protection as 2026 Elections Approach
item.description: A new national study examining political opposition and civic engagement within Black communities has found that Black voters are signaling dissatisfaction, caution and conditional readiness to act as the 2026 elections approach, with economic strain and fear of retaliation being major barriers to participation. The post Black Voters Demand Results and Protection as 2026 Elections Approach appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: DC Water Updates Community in Forum Regarding Potomac Interceptor Collapse
item.description: DC Water and Maryland held community forums to address residents' concerns about the Jan. 19 Potomac Interceptor collapse and wastewater overflow, and to provide updates on the rehabilitation and restoration plans for the affected area. The post DC Water Updates Community in Forum Regarding Potomac Interceptor Collapse appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Live Boldly – March 2026 Message From Department of Aging and Community Living
item.description: The Department of Aging and Community Living (DACL) has been working hard to provide vital services to seniors in the District, including providing nearly 900,000 meals in Fiscal Year 2025, expanding nutrition services, and protecting vulnerable adults from abuse and neglect. The post Live Boldly – March 2026 Message From Department of Aging and Community Living appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Women’s History Month: Estate Planning as an Act of Self-Care
item.description: Estate planning is an essential form of self-care for women, particularly Black women, as it provides protection, dignity, and peace of mind, while also preserving generational wealth and ensuring that loved ones are not left guessing or fighting in court. The post Women’s History Month: Estate Planning as an Act of Self-Care appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: U.S. Casualties Mount as D.C. Tightens Security Following Iran Strikes
item.description: President Trump launched a war with Iran without congressional approval, resulting in the deaths of three U.S. service members and scores of civilians, prompting criticism from politicians and organizations for undermining democratic checks and balances. item.title: Maryland Political Updates: Hakeem Jeffries Talks Redistricting; Moore’s Housing Agenda Moves Forward
item.description: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries discussed redistricting with Senate President Bill Ferguson, but the proposed plan is opposed by multiple Senate Democrats and does not have the support to pass in the Senate. item.title: Amid Fletcher-Johnson Redevelopment, Community Members Remember the Good Times
item.description: Dr. George H. Rutherford, former principal of Fletcher-Johnson Middle School, maintained contact with his former students and was honored at a party organized by alumni, who remember him as a courageous leader who provided them with support and structure.
